lead: Hewlett Packard Enterprise fell 16.33% to $40.18 the day after record quarterly sales of $14.5B (+50%), because a bigger share of low-margin AI servers and part costs outrunning prices cut its gross margin; the biggest non-chip big-tech move on a day the Nasdaq fell 1.48% as chips gave back Monday's rally.
why: Margins, not sales: Q4 revenue $14.55B (+50.3%) beat the $14.45B consensus and EPS $1.43 beat $1.29, but non-GAAP gross margin fell 2.2 points from the prior quarter to 38.2% on a higher mix of AI servers and costs rising faster than pricing, per CFO Marie Myers (StockStory via TradingView); she expects gross margin to moderate as fiscal 2027 progresses and AI server volumes (incl. Helios) ramp (Finwire/Invezz).

Supply: CEO Antonio Neri said HPE operates in a 'significantly supply-constrained environment' and expects memory, NAND and other critical components to stay constrained to at least the second half of calendar 2028 (Finwire/Invezz). Orders +88%, AI backlog a record $10.5B.

Context: still about +66% year to date and ~45% under its $73.46 October high (StockStory). Market: S&P 500 -0.50% (7,201.09), Nasdaq -1.48%, Dow +0.85% to 50,018.70; Nvidia -5.86%, Micron -11%, Analog Devices -17.4%; Apple +1.4%, Microsoft +0.7%, Meta -1.3%, Amazon -1.2%, Alphabet -1.1%; Kohl's +19.5%, Dollar Tree +11.2% on earnings (Motley Fool, StockTitan). Next: October PCE Wed Nov 25; markets closed Thursday.
